_comment: Shared vectors for the T-of-N signer-counting rule, read by all three suites: js/test.mjs,
The rule is implemented three times, in three languages, ~90 lines each. Nothing but a shared fixture
keeps them answering the same question - a divergence between two of them is invisible to a suite that
only exercises one, and was in fact found by review rather than by CI.
Keys are derived deterministically so every language builds the same addresses without shipping any
secret: private key i is the byte (i+1) repeated 32 times. Signatures are recoverable secp256k1 over
keccak256(message) with no Ethereum prefix, which is what the engine produces.
'signers' is how many addresses the signer list holds, ordered as the verifier contract stores them:
every operator instance first, then every Soda instance, so the last N entries are Soda's - one per
evaluator - and within either block entry i belongs to evaluator i % N.
'signedBy' are positions in that list, not key indices.
